title: DARE: Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement
title_zh: DARE：面向修复增强的难度分析

paragraphs.en: DARE框架通过预测修复任务难度并提供任务特定支持，显著提升编程智能体的修复成功率。 LLM-based coding agents are primarily evaluated by their solve rates. However, this metric does not reveal how difficult the solved tasks are or account for differences in task difficulty across benchmarks. Determining the difficulty of individual tasks by repeatedly running multiple agents is costly, while a predicted difficulty score alone provides limited guidance on what support an agent needs. To address these challenges, we propose DARE (Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement), which integrates repair-task difficulty measurement, prediction, feature-group contribution analysis, and task-specific repair support. We define continuous task difficulty as the observed failure rate across multiple coding agents. The DARE difficulty model predicts this difficulty using 151 static features extracted from benchmark artifacts. The framework also analyzes the contributions of seven Repair-Task Feature Groups to identify the characteristics most salient to each task and uses this information to select task-specific agent support. We evaluate DARE on four benchmark partitions comprising 2,594 tasks. The difficulty model's aligned predictions achieve Spearman's $ρ$ = .476-.621 on held-out partitions, and the most salient Feature Groups vary across tasks and benchmarks. Furthermore, coding-agent experiments show that matching support to each task's salient Feature Group raises repair success from 54.7% to 79.6% on nine high-difficulty tasks. These findings demonstrate that difficulty prediction and interpretation can lead to practical improvements in automated program repair (APR), while also providing a basis for difficulty-stratified agent evaluation, cross-benchmark comparisons, and identifying areas of repair capability that warrant further improvement.
paragraphs.zh: DARE框架通过预测修复任务难度并提供任务特定支持，显著提升编程智能体的修复成功率。 基于大语言模型的编程智能体主要以解题率作为评估指标。 然而，该指标无法揭示已解决任务的难度如何，也无法考虑不同基准之间任务难度的差异。 通过反复运行多个智能体来确定单个任务的难度成本高昂，而仅凭预测的难度分数又难以指导应该为智能体提供何种支持。 为应对这些挑战，我们提出了DARE（Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement，面向修复增强的难度分析），它集成了修复任务难度度量、预测、特征组贡献分析以及任务特定的修复支持。 我们将连续的任务难度定义为多个编程智能体上观察到的失败率。 DARE难度模型利用从基准产物中提取的151个静态特征来预测该难度。 该框架还分析了七个修复任务特征组的贡献，以识别对每个任务最显著的特征，并利用这些信息为智能体选择任务特定的支持。 我们在包含2,594个任务的四个基准分区上评估了DARE。 难度模型的对齐预测在留出分区上达到Spearman's $ρ$ = .476-.621，且最显著的特征组因任务和基准而异。 此外，编程智能体实验表明，根据每个任务最显著的特征组来匹配支持，可将九个高难度任务上的修复成功率从54.7%提升至79.6%。 这些发现表明，难度预测与解释能够为自动化程序修复（APR）带来实际改进，同时为难度分层的智能体评估、跨基准比较以及识别值得进一步改进的修复能力领域提供了基础。
